item.title: Colin Kaepernick is still upset that his mom wanted him to date Taylor Swift, a White woman
item.description: Colin Kaepernick's memoir reveals his mother once urged him to ask out Taylor Swift, a story he and Jemele Hill discussed at a Detroit event.
item.content:encoded:
Saturday night, Colin Kaepernick and Jemele Hill spoke at the National Black Footwear Forum in Detroit, Michigan. Their conversation focused primarily on, you guessed it, racism, as well as Kaepernick’s life and upcoming memoir, "The Perilous Fight."

OutKick reporters attended the event, which did not permit questions.

One topic, in particular, caught our attention. Hill told Kaepernick that she was struck by a story in his memoir about the time his mother wanted him to date Taylor Swift.

Hill and Kaepernick lamented that his mother wanted him to be with a girl like Swift, with the implication he wasn't interested in white women.

OutKick obtained a copy of Kaepernick’s new book, in which he tells that story about his mother and Swift:

"Now that I had my own car, it was time for me to embrace another teenage rite of passage: a girlfriend. I started seeing a very cute Black girl named Crystal. Right away, I noticed how different I felt with her than in my own home. I could talk to Crystal, really talk to her, without having to explain myself; it was a remarkable discovery, being understood up front and without question. When I visited her home, I was stunned by how warm and welcoming her family was. I immediately felt comfortable there," he begins.

"I asked Crystal to the homecoming dance, a formal affair involving fancy gowns, tuxedoes, and corsages. We had a nice time at the dance. When I got the official portrait from that night, featuring me and Crystal posed up in that classic, airbrushed frame, my mother hid it away in the back of a drawer."

"My mother convinced me to ask Lindsay, the daughter of one of her friends, to the next formal dance. Lindsay was white. When I brought that picture home, my mother promptly plastered it on the wall for all to see. In her mind, Crystal was just a phase. Lindsay was the kind of girl I should want.

"It was disappointing to me that my mother didn't seem capable of seeing who I really was. Years later, when I was in the NFL, she told me that I should ask out Taylor Swift (long before Travis Kelce made his move) because we would be perfect together. No slight to Taylor, but she was not my type. Crystal was also an athlete, a basketball player, and track runner so it was hard for us to find time for each other during basketball season. I was always on my way to practice or a game.

Oh, the horror of a mother encouraging her professional athlete son to ask out one of the most famous women in America, who was around his age. A white girl, even.

ESPN HOPES TO MAKE PETER SCHRAGER ITS FIRST HOMEGROWN STAR IN OVER A DECADE | BOBBY BURACK

During multiple portions of the conversation Saturday night, Kaepernick spoke negatively about two white parents raising him.

He repeatedly claimed that they did not understand or support his "blackness." He also said they did not support his national anthem protest when it began.

How dare two parents refuse to support their son’s decision to disrespect the American flag and encourage him to date Taylor Swift?

How Kaepernick ever made it to the NFL despite this type of parenting is apparently the story of a true underdog.

Colin Kaepernick is still upset that his mom wanted him to date Taylor Swift, a white woman.

Of course, Hill did not challenge Kaepernick on any of these points. Rather, she opened the discussion by blaming injuries for Kaepernick’s poor play and calling on the Atlanta Falcons to consider signing him to play quarterback in 2026.

Finally, say what you will about Travis Kelce, but Swift should be glad Kaepernick stopped taking dating advice from his white mother.

item.title: Betting Preview: Arizona Diamondbacks host Miami Marlins with both teams still chasing slim postseason hopes
item.description: Sandy Alcantara faces Corbin Burnes as the Miami Marlins and Arizona Diamondbacks clash with slim postseason hopes on the line in this matchup.
item.content:encoded:
We head back to the diamond now that we have just one football game on the agenda. With only about 12 games remaining for most teams, we are squarely locked into the final lap of the playoff race. As you'd expect, there are a lot of teams that are pretty much out of it at this point, and a few that still have an outside shot at making it to the postseason. Tonight, the Marlins and Diamondbacks, who both have a slim chance of making the postseason, square off.

The Miami Marlins have a few things left to play for this postseason. They are currently still alive in the postseason race, but going 3-7 over their past ten games has hindered any real possibility of making it. They are 7.5 games back of the final spot in the postseason, which means they need to overcome the Pirates, Diamondbacks, and Padres in 12 games to win the final spot. This can be looked at as a stepping stone year, but you'd have to have confidence that the Marlins will do something in the offseason to further advance the club.

Personally, I think they are likely to trade away guys instead of signing someone to help them. That's pretty normal for the Miami franchise, though. One guy who they have an option on, and I assume they will pick up, is tonight's starter, Sandy Alcantara. He had some strong moments for the team this season with a 13-10 record, 3.78 ERA, and a 1.22 WHIP. He has struggled a bit on the road with a 4.32 road ERA. It has been a rough stretch for him, though, as he has allowed 15 earned runs over the past three starts. Collectively, the Diamondbacks have hit .207 against him in 82 at-bats.

The Arizona Diamondbacks still have hope for this postseason run. Their hope is a bit more realistic than that of their opponent. They are just 2.5 games behind the Padres, and they have their final three games of the season against their divisional foes. The Diamondbacks have been pretty reliable to bettors and have looked great most of this season. Their offense is sharp, and their pitching staff doesn't have a ton of names that stand out to you, but they do get the job done.

Diamondbacks star spotted at casino during team's game after no-showing to stadium earlier in the week

Tonight, they have one guy who has a history of being one of the best in the game: Corbin Burnes. This is just his second start since returning from injury, but should the Diamondbacks make it to the postseason, he will likely have four starts total under his belt and be in a good position to help the club. In his start against the Royals, Burnes went three innings, allowed two hits, two walks, and had two strikeouts. He didn't allow a run. This was his first action in over a year, so that's good news. The Marlins have only had three hitters see him in 10 at-bats, and he has allowed just two singles.

This is not a game that I can trust the Marlins to win, unfortunately. They are playing some pretty poor baseball right now, and Alcantara has looked rough. He's had a lot of good stretches, but he's also had some really tough outings, especially lately. The Diamondbacks have a slightly better bullpen, and I think their offense is better, so I'm going to take the Diamondbacks in this one. I do have a slight lean to the under, if that helps at all.

item.title: Iran’s proxy money machine: How the Houthis built a multibillion-dollar network despite US sanctions
item.description: The Houthis' advance toward the Bab el-Mandeb Strait is fueled by a sprawling sanctions-evasion network spanning Iranian oil, crypto and Russia.
item.content:encoded:
The Houthis’ rapid advance toward one of the world’s most important shipping chokepoints is putting fresh scrutiny on the sprawling financial network that has helped transform the Iran-backed group from a Yemeni insurgency into a heavily armed regional power capable of threatening global trade.

The group has seized new territory along Yemen’s Red Sea coast, including the strategic port city of Mocha, and expanded toward the Bab el-Mandeb Strait. The waterway connects the Red Sea to the Gulf of Aden and carries a significant share of global maritime trade and energy shipments.

For the Trump administration, the Houthi advance is becoming as much a financial challenge as a military one. Washington is intensifying efforts to choke off the money sustaining Iran and its proxies, but the Houthis have built a sprawling sanctions-evasion network while controlling ports, trade routes and millions of Yemenis — raising a difficult question for Treasury: how do you cut off the cash fueling the group without cutting off food, fuel and other lifelines to civilians?

SAUDI ARABIA TELLS TRUMP NOW IS THE TIME FOR MILITARY ACTION AS IRAN-BACKED HOUTHIS ADVANCE

The Houthis operate a financial network that extends far beyond Yemen, according to Adam Rousselle, founder of Between the Lines Research. 

"We’re dealing with a very well-capitalized group," Rousselle told Fox News Digital.

In a 2025 investigation for the Global Network on Extremism and Technology, Rousselle traced a financing system spanning Houthi-controlled ports, tariffs, Iranian oil, informal hawala networks, cryptocurrency exchanges and foreign facilitators across Russia, Turkey and Southeast Asia.

Control of ports has historically been central to Houthi revenue because Yemen depends heavily on imports. Rousselle’s GNET report said the Houthis have imposed steep fees at ports they control and tariffs on goods brought into their territory from rival Yemeni ports.

HOUTHIS ENTER US 'KILL BOX' AFTER SEIZING RED SEA 'CORK,' FORMER PENTAGON OFFICIAL WARNS

The group’s latest territorial gains could strengthen that economic base even further.

Nadwa Al-Dawsari, a Yemen expert and associate fellow at the Middle East Institute, told lawmakers in Sept. 1 testimony before the House Foreign Affairs Committee that territory is central to the Houthis’ ability to withstand outside pressure.

"The most important source of that leverage is territory," Al-Dawsari testified. "The Houthis have been able to consolidate their power and build increasingly sophisticated military capabilities because they control significant territory, a large population, ports, infrastructure, and resources."

"That territorial base allows them to recruit, generate revenue, manufacture and store weapons, control smuggling routes, and regenerate capabilities degraded by airstrikes and sanctions," she added.

IRAN LOSES KEY ECONOMIC LIFELINE IN MIDDLE EAST THAT TRUMP'S SANCTIONS COULDN'T REACH AS DEADLOCK PERSISTS

Rousselle said the Houthis’ finances should not be understood simply as Tehran handing cash to an Iranian proxy.

"It’s a bit of a misunderstanding that the Iranians just give them money," he said, describing the Houthis instead as embedded in a broader Iranian commercial ecosystem.

"The Houthis aren't sanctions-proof; they're sanctions-adapted," Miad Maleki, senior fellow at the Foundation for Defense of Democracies, told Fox News Digital. "Most of their money is made inside Yemen — customs and taxes at Hodeidah and Ras Isa, and fuel above all."

Treasury has estimated that the Houthis generate more than $2 billion a year from oil sales, while Iran provides the group with a free monthly oil shipment through Iranian-owned or affiliated companies based in Dubai. Treasury has also documented Houthi revenue from taxes imposed on petroleum imports.

CHINA ORDERS FIRMS TO IGNORE US IRAN SANCTIONS, DARING US TO ENFORCE CRACKDOWN

"Sanctions can't reach domestic extraction," Maleki said. "What they can reach is the plumbing between Sana'a and the outside world; the exchange houses, the Dubai and Muscat correspondents, the tankers and the wallets."

At the center of that system is Sa’id al-Jamal, whom the Treasury Department has identified as an Iran-backed Houthi financial official operating an international network that sells Iranian commodities and channels proceeds toward the group.

Treasury said in April 2025 that al-Jamal’s network had procured tens of millions of dollars in weapons, sensitive goods and commodities from Russia and identified eight digital-asset wallets used by the Houthis. Blockchain analytics cited in Rousselle’s GNET research identified nearly $900 million in outflows across those addresses.

Rousselle cautioned against treating that figure as a complete picture of Houthi wealth.

"The system is more important than the number itself," he said, describing the network as fluid and difficult to quantify.

Russia, he argued, has become a particularly significant part of the network. "The Russians are definitely more hands-on in their support," Rousselle said.

TRUMP TO CONFRONT XI AT HIGH-STAKES SUMMIT OVER CHINA BACKING FOR IRAN, RUSSIA

Al-Dawsari’s congressional testimony similarly highlighted the Houthis’ expanding relationships beyond Iran, saying the group is "deepening ties with other U.S. adversaries, particularly Russia and China."

She cited reports that Russia provided targeting data used to help the Houthis attack Western ships in the Red Sea and that Russian petroleum products were transferred ship-to-ship into a Houthi-controlled tanker before reaching the Houthi-controlled port of Ras Isa.

The China connection is more complicated. Rousselle said Chinese-linked private commercial actors appear in parts of the network but distinguished that activity from proven direct Chinese government involvement.

"The Chinese are kind of… turning a blind eye," he said.

His GNET report described Iranian oil flowing to privately owned Chinese "teapot" refineries and examined transactions linked to Southeast Asian financial networks, while cautioning that the available evidence did not establish direct Chinese government control of Houthi financing.

Al-Dawsari pointed to a broader Chinese role in Houthi supply chains. Citing U.S. officials, she said a Chinese satellite company with ties to the Chinese military provided satellite imagery supporting Houthi attacks against U.S. warships and international shipping. She also cited interdiction data showing that 60% of the components and materials used in the Houthi Qasef-2K drone came from China, compared with roughly 15% from Iran.

That sprawling network is now testing Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent’s broader effort to isolate Tehran economically and disrupt the financial channels sustaining Iran and its proxies.

Rousselle said decentralized illicit-finance networks present a fundamental challenge.

"You’re dealing with a ‘you shut down one, another pops up’ kind of situation," he said.

Maleki argued that Washington should concentrate on the points where Houthi money intersects with the formal financial system.

IRAN TAPS FINANCIAL LIFELINE, RUSSIAN ARMS AS TRUMP ESCALATES 'CRUSHING' ECONOMIC WARFARE

"The soft spots are wherever Houthi money touches the formal system," he said. "Treasury has named the Yemeni banks and the Sana'a exchange houses that pay for missile components; it should now name the foreign correspondents still clearing for them. That is the one tool that changes behavior overnight."

Oman represents another potential pressure point. "Oman is the Houthis' land bridge and their mailing address," Maleki said.

But squeezing Houthi finances presents another dilemma: Yemen remains one of the world’s most fragile humanitarian environments, and the Houthis control ports and infrastructure through which civilians receive food, fuel and other basic goods.

"I would be lying if I had a concrete answer to it," Rousselle said when asked how Washington could disrupt Houthi revenue without worsening the humanitarian crisis.

IRAN-BACKED HOUTHI THREAT IN RED SEA COULD LEAD TO MAJOR US POLICY SHIFT, ANALYSTS SAY

"The humanitarian argument is the Houthis' best shield, and it's backwards," Maleki said. "Food and medicine are licensed and should stay that way."

"Keep the goods flowing and take away the toll," he added, arguing that Washington should seek ways to prevent humanitarian trade from generating taxes and fees for Houthi authorities.

Rousselle warned that the challenge extends far beyond Yemen.

"This isn’t just about the Houthis," he said. "This is about any sanctioned actor worldwide capable of harnessing financial systems that are completely outside of regulatory control."

The Treasury Department did not immediately respond to Fox News Digital’s request for comment.

item.title: Danny DeVito exposes wild party scene on 1980s 'Taxi' set: 'Crudité and cocaine'
item.description: Danny DeVito revealed the wild after-hours "Taxi" ragers featured "crudité and cocaine," with Robin Williams and Michael Jackson among the guests.
item.content:encoded:
When the cameras stopped rolling on "Taxi," Danny DeVito and his co-stars apparently shifted into a very different gear.

DeVito recalled cast members and celebrity guests spilling into all-night "ragers" where music blared until sunrise and, as he put it, there was "crudité and cocaine." 

"But getting back to the parties, those were like ragers," he explained during an appearance on the "All the Smoke" podcast. "Like we would have like, crudité and cocaine... basically it was the '80s. It was like, really crazy."

'DEADPOOL' STAR RYAN REYNOLDS TORCHES 1980S NOSTALGIA, CALLS DECADE A ‘F---ING MESS’ PEOPLE ‘FORGET’

And the guest list extended well beyond the "Taxi" cast.

"...people would come from like, 'Laverne & Shirley' would come and watch our show. And Robin Williams would come," he remembered. "And we had visitors from outside who was a big fan of the show – Michael Jackson would come.

"He would sit up in the booth, not with the audience, sit up in the booth and watch. Lots of people came. Belushi, you know, people from 'SNL' in the early days."

DeVito said the celebration kicked into high gear as soon as the night's work was finished.

"So then we would transition right from the show that we finished, like, 10:30, 11. And immediately go up and blare the music... until the sun came up," he recalled.

"We had to be to work on Monday at noon," DeVito said. "That's all we had to care about."

DeVito became a household name as the hilariously abrasive Louie De Palma on "Taxi," the hit sitcom that ran from 1978 to 1983. The show featured an ensemble cast that included Judd Hirsch as Alex Reiger, Marilu Henner as Elaine Nardo, Tony Danza as Tony Banta, Christopher Lloyd as Jim Ignatowski, Jeff Conaway as Bobby Wheeler and Andy Kaufman as Latka Gravas.

"And it was one of the greatest experiences for the beginning of anybody's career, because you were working with writers who were nose to the grindstone, never give up, dedicated, funny a-- people. And they never let you down. And they work until an hour before the show with you."

After "Taxi," DeVito built an unusually versatile career as an actor, director and producer.

His most recognizable acting projects include "Twins," "Batman Returns" and "Matilda."

item.title: Abdul El-Sayed protested against 'ex-terrorists' who converted to Christianity, unearthed report reveals
item.description: Democratic Senate nominee Abdul El-Sayed led a 2007 University of Michigan protest against ex-terrorists who discussed converting to Christianity.
item.content:encoded:
Michigan’s progressive Democratic Senate nominee, while sitting atop an organization with ties to an alleged terrorist group, once protested an event where a trio of "ex-terrorists" discussed their conversion to Christianity.

Abdul El-Sayed, who is running in Michigan’s highly watched and hotly contested race for Senate against the GOP nominee, former Rep. Mike Rogers, was a leader of a protest against three "ex-terrorists" who spoke at the University of Michigan in 2007, according to an unearthed report.

The protest, chronicled by the Michigan Daily, was against three speakers, Walid Shoebat, Zachariah Annani and Kamal Saleem, self-described former terrorists who were making the rounds during the mid-2000s to discuss their lives in the Palestine Liberation Organization and the Muslim Brotherhood before converting to Christianity.

TOP GOP SENATOR REVEALS WHAT DEM COLLEAGUES ARE FRETTING ABOUT BEHIND CLOSED DOORS

Students attending the talk staged a walkout, which El-Sayed cheered afterward.

"We’ve done something good today, and we need to keep that going in the future," El-Sayed said.

El-Sayed's campaign spokesperson, Cole Wozniak, told Fox News Digital that the candidate had "unequivocally denounced terrorism."

"Two decades ago, he protested against speakers who have been widely condemned by experts, including in national security, for spreading misinformation and fabricating their backstories," Wozniak said. "Mike Rogers and his allies are pushing lies because they don't want to talk about the record-high prices Michiganders are paying for gas and groceries because of Trump's illegal war in Iran."

There are also questions about the backgrounds of Shoebat, Annani and Saleem. The New York Times reported in 2008 that before speaking at the Air Force Academy, organizations criticized their appearance and several Arab-American civil rights organizations questioned why they had not been arrested or deported given their apparent connections to terrorist groups.

Event organizers told the Michigan Daily that it was meant to educate people about the dangers of Muslim extremism, not promote intolerance. On the other hand, the protesters, who were clad in yellow, argued that their pushback was highlighting that the event was "generalizing an entire group of people."

SCHUMER DUCKS QUESTION ON CAMPAIGNING WITH SOCIALIST CANDIDATE WHO REFUSES TO BACK HIM AS LEADER

El-Sayed at the time was the vice president of the Muslim Students Association (MSA), which is alleged to have ties to the Muslim Brotherhood, an organization that the White House requested last year that the State and Treasury departments determine whether certain chapters should be designated as foreign terrorist organizations and specially designated global terrorists.

By the early 1960s, the Muslim Brotherhood had built a presence in the U.S., where its members functioned primarily through student unions on college campuses, most particularly through the Muslim Students Association (MSA).

Lara Burns, a senior research fellow at George Washington University’s program on extremism, told the Senate Judiciary Committee last month in written testimony that by the 1960s, the Muslim Brotherhood had built a presence in the U.S., "where its members functioned primarily through student unions on college campuses, most particularly through the Muslim Students Association (MSA)."

SENATE MAP TIGHTENS AS TOP FORECASTER MOVES 3 RACES TOWARD DEMOCRATS

The MSA did not immediately respond to a request for comment.

President Donald Trump’s administration has sought to label a handful of chapters of the Muslim Brotherhood as foreign terrorist organizations and specially designated global terrorists.

Trump ordered that the Lebanese Muslim Brotherhood chapter, Jordanian Muslim Brotherhood chapter and Egyptian Muslim Brotherhood chapter be considered for the designations for their connections to Hamas and the Oct. 7, 2023, attack on Israel.

item.title: Judge Adam Levy previews his ‘nitty-gritty’ new show – and how his style compares to his mom Judge Judy
item.description: Judge Adam Levy says he "learned from the best" as his mom Judge Judy Sheindlin created "Adam's Law," premiering Sept. 14 in national syndication.
item.content:encoded:
STAMFORD, CT — Judge Adam Levy’s new courtroom show "Adam’s Law" premieres this month, and he feels prepared because he "learned from the best," his mom Judge Judy Sheindlin.

Sheindlin’s popular show "Judge Judy" ran for over 25 years. She's now passing the baton to her son, who has also starred in courtroom shows like "Justice on Trial" and "Tribunal Justice." 

Before bringing his talents to television, Levy served two terms as Putnam County district attorney in New York. He was one of three adjudicating judges on "Tribunal," but he’ll be the lone judge at the helm for CBS Media Ventures' "Adam’s Law," premiering Monday.

"Well, we dive into the nitty-gritty," Judge Adam Levy told Fox News Digital at Stamford Studios following a taping of the show this summer. 

JUDGE JUDY'S SON, FELLOW JUDGES DISH ON WHY AUDIENCES LOVE TV COURTROOM DRAMA: INSTANT ACCOUNTABILITY

"We get into the details. The devil’s always in those details. And so we make sure that the information that we have isn’t just limited to what the litigants tell us in a complaint or an answer. When appropriate, we will look into backgrounds to ensure what they tell us is corroborated or if we can contradict it, we will. So the right person wins, the right person loses," he added.

Two women became visibly emotional during the two cases Levy presided over that morning, sharing their testimonies through tears. While Levy said he understands that these are real people with feelings, he aims to focus on the facts and not the emotions.

"The law is about facts," Levy said. "The law doesn’t have much to do with feelings. I tell that to my family all the time – my facts don’t care about your feelings. Listen, these are real cases, they’re real people. And many of them come here, and they’re committed to their cause. They feel strongly. The ones we had today were high-dollar values, but it could be a $50 case, it could be a $100 case, it doesn’t make a difference.

JUDGE JUDY'S SON ADAM LEVY SAYS HE COULD FIX LOS ANGELES 'IN A MONTH'

"The plaintiffs feel wronged, and they want justice. And when they really start getting emotional, you see that. You see that whatever happened to them really bothered them. I take their cases seriously. They come to us and waive their right to be heard in small claims court, and allow me to adjudicate the cases for them. Why would I give them anything less than my full attention and true justice?"

Levy said he knew he was ready for his own show "when Judge Judy told me I was ready for my own show."

"I was very happy to go back to Wyoming, going skiing, but it was time," he shared. "She wanted to reassess what she was doing, and thinking about maybe hanging up her gavel, and she felt as though it was time. It was time for me that I had developed whatever skills she thought were necessary…"

"I don’t want to disappoint her," he joked. "I don’t want the word ‘bupkis’ next to my name in the will."

Levy described his courtroom style as "similar" to his mom’s.

"We both can’t stand nonsense," he said. "If you’re going to come in, and you’re going to lie, neither of us really have much tolerance for that, patience for it… Come to the court, tell the truth. A trial is supposed to be a search for the truth and not about who can tell a better lie. That’s what we’re all about."

FORMER PROSECUTOR ADAM LEVY SENDS WARNING FOR KNICKS PARADE SAFETY AFTER NYC CHAOS

Growing up, he admitted he didn’t always appreciate his mom's work schedule and his life as a latchkey kid as Judge Judy juggled her responsibilities.

Now he admires her work ethic, saying she passed it down to him, and he hopes to do the same for his kids.

Levy quipped that his kids think he's "crazy" because of the hours of prep he does each week for the show, but he wants to be prepared for the litigants who called him for help.

"It’s much easier when you love what you do," he said.

"Adam’s Law" was created by Judge Judy Sheindlin. It is produced by her Queen Bee Productions and premiered Monday in national syndication.

item.title: WWE star Nattie shares insight on The Undertaker’s booking style in AAA
item.description: Nattie reveals The Undertaker's unique booking style at AAA, describing his love for aggression and intensity that sets him apart from other WWE creatives.
item.content:encoded:
The Undertaker ruled the WWE ring for decades as he developed his "Dead Man" persona and put the fear into any of his opponents that would step up to him.

Those days are a thing of the past and The Undertaker has since switched his role from fearsome in-ring competitor to one of the creatives behind the AAA promotion in Mexico.

COMPLETE PRO WRESTLING COVERAGE ON OUTKICK

The WWE legend has been among the minds behind AAA’s rise to prominence on the pro wrestling scene. Nattie, a legend in her own right, praised Undertaker for the creative direction he’s undertaken at AAA.

"’Taker is the man. Everybody loves working for ‘Taker. That’s why I think everybody that goes there like Chelsea Green has gone on the record saying, ‘I want to work for ‘Taker.’ She said she would text ‘Taker and ask him please let me do AAA," she told OutKick Dropkick. "And same with Roxanne (Perez), I know she wanted to do AAA.

"‘Taker has really elevated that promotion, along with Jeremy Borash who helps Undertaker run AAA with the family that had run it before WWE stepped in – they still kept management, they still kept people, they still kept the family. But ‘Taker has been involved, WWE has been involved, Jeremy Borash – they just elevated it."

Nattie noted that The Undertaker is different creatively from a Shawn Michaels, who helps run NXT, and Triple H (Paul Levesque), who is the Chief Content Officer for WWE.

"And so, the coolest thing about Undertaker is that his style is very different as a booker. It’s very different than Shawn Michaels. It’s very different than Triple H. But it doesn’t mean that any one of them is better than the other," she said. "It just means that ‘Taker has a different style.

"He loves aggression. He loves intensity. He loves selling. I like to say ‘Taker kinda loves violence. He’s just such a cool boss. He’ll give us advice, he’ll give us feedback but he also gives us support and encouragement and he really believes in us. And that’s so important. And he’s communicative. He was helping me for my entrance for last year’s Triplemania. He was helping me with different ideas. He’s the man."

item.title: Bob Mackie, legendary designer who dressed Cher, Tina Turner and Dolly Parton, dead at 87
item.description: Bob Mackie's iconic designs for Cher, Carol Burnett and Diana Ross shaped Hollywood glamour, while stars like Sabrina Carpenter revived his archives.
item.content:encoded:
Bob Mackie, the legendary fashion and costume designer known for dressing some of the biggest stars, died Monday. He was 87

"It is with a heavy heart that we share the news that Mr. Bob Mackie passed away today," a post shared on his official Instagram read. "He lived his 87 years to the fullest, fulfilling his dream of being a Fashion and Costume Designer, which is all he ever wanted to do."

"His genius and extraordinary designs will live on forever, continuing to bring beauty into this world," the statement concluded.

item.title: Far-left attack backfires spectacularly as radical online personality whines after attacking female Trump aide
item.description: Aaron Rupar faces White House backlash after attacking a female press wrangler in a C-SPAN clip from President Trump's Ireland departure.
item.content:encoded:
A self-styled leftist journalist who chronicles President Donald Trump's moves online is crying foul after he made another attack on a young female Trump staffer, part of a pattern he's been engaged in for weeks.

"another [sic] blonde Trump flunkie starts literally shoving photographers away from Trump," Aaron Rupar posted on his X account on Sunday afternoon, attaching a clip from C-SPAN showing Trump greeting family members next to Air Force 1 as he prepared to board the plane leaving Ireland.

The clip shows Ellie Acra, a White House press wrangler, sternly directing the media to exit the area underneath the wing of the plane, using the often-employed phrase: "Thank you, press."

White House press wranglers are the grunt of the press office, responsible for herding the media to and from designated areas where they are covering the president. The wranglers are key members in Republican and Democrat administrations alike in keeping the president on schedule.

EL-SAYED DRAGGED OVER ‘WEIRD’ FIXATION ON ‘TALKING ABOUT OTHER PEOPLE’S WIVES’ AFTER LATEST TRUMP ATTACK

The clip and Rupar's commentary on it quickly went viral as users, including the White House, came out en masse to defend the young White House staffer and rail against the left-wing personality.

The White House's rapid response X account responded to Rupar, who in recent weeks has repeatedly tracked and commented on the movements of embattled White House aide Natalie Harp.

"This is a press wrangler doing her job — and doing it well. Aaron, meanwhile, is gutter trash (in his 40s) who spends his days hiding behind his keyboard and making disturbing comments about women doing their jobs. Truly a sick freak!" the White House account said.

Following that response, Rupar whined online and suggested that the White House was inciting harassment and threats against him.

"For the second straight day, the White House's taxpayer-funded incitement account is attacking me and oddly mentioning I'm in my 40s (which I know makes me way too old for the president) When they do this it results in a flood of harassing and threatening messages, which of course is the point," he said.

DEM’S ‘SEXIST’ REMARK AGAINST CANCER SURVIVOR PROVOKES REPUBLICAN TO GO SCORCHED EARTH: ‘GUY’S GOT A PROBLEM’

Rupar found himself in the White House's crosshairs on Saturday, too, that time for posting another photo of Harp. He and other online leftist have been insinuating for weeks, without evidence, that Harp and Trump are engaged in an inappropriate relationship.

"Look who made the trip to Ireland!" Rupar said in a post, adding a photo of Harp and a hashtag, #TravelWithNatalie, which he has used while tracking Harp's movements with Trump.

The White House noted in its response that the president's aides, unsurprisingly, travel with him.

"President Trump does, in fact, travel with staff. Aaron, on the other hand, is a sick, deluded freak (in his 40s) who sits behind a keyboard and posts creepy things like this," the post said.

JON OSSOFF DODGES ON WHY HE INVOKED TRUMP AIDE'S NAME DURING GEORGIA CAMPAIGN RALLY

item.title: Inside House Republicans' plan to end run Dem opposition and pass Trump-backed voter ID
item.description: Congressional Republicans plan to bypass the Senate filibuster and pass the SAVE America Act's voter ID and proof of citizenship rules via reconciliation.
item.content:encoded:
Congressional Republicans have a plan to pass key portions of the Safeguarding American Voter Eligibility (SAVE) America Act before the end of this year.

The election integrity bill backed by President Donald Trump and fiercely opposed by Democrats has stalled in Congress, where Senate Majority Leader John Thune, R-S.D., has been reluctant to call it up for a vote, given that it's all but assured to fail.

At least several Democrats would be needed to reach the Senate's 60-vote threshold to break a filibuster. But left-wing lawmakers in the House and Senate have panned the legislation as an attempt to sow doubt in U.S. elections at best and voter suppression at worst.

Speaker Mike Johnson, R-La., is now pushing Republicans to pass the bill's main mandates via the budget reconciliation process, which allows the party in power to pass sweeping fiscal policy without input from the minority due to its sidelining of the Senate filibuster. Rep. Bryan Steil, R-Wis., chairman of the Committee on House Administration, is tasked with overseeing how that part of the bill gets done.

TRUMP QUESTIONS THUNE'S LEADERSHIP AS SAVE AMERICA ACT STALLS

"I'd rather pass the SAVE America Act. But recognizing that the Senate might not be able to get that done with the 60-vote threshold, let's leverage the parliamentary procedure, bring that threshold down to 50, and get some really commonsense reforms done," Steil told Fox News Digital in an interview. "I've been having great conversations with my colleagues in the administration as well as the Senate."

SENATE FACES 'COME-TO-JESUS' MOMENT ON TRUMP'S ELECTION PRIORITY UNDER GOP'S NEW PLAN

Steil told Fox News Digital that he hoped Congress could pass a reconciliation bill with SAVE America before the November midterm elections, but conceded "the clock is ticking down pretty quickly."

The budget reconciliation process is a lengthy one, with Republicans having taken roughly half a year to use it to pass Trump's signature One Big, Beautiful Bill Act last year. Both the House and Senate must pass budget "frameworks," with instructions for relevant committees to enact policies that either spend or cut funding to a specified amount.

Those committees pass their portions, then send them back to the House and Senate budget committees to tie them together into one massive bill. Identical bills must pass the House and Senate before getting to Trump's desk.

Steil's panel, which has jurisdiction over federal election law, is aiming to include two portions of the original SAVE America Act: a proof of citizenship mandate for the voter registration process, and a nationwide photo ID rule to cast a ballot.

READ THE DOCUMENTS: WHITE HOUSE RELEASES ELECTION INTEGRITY FILES AFTER TRUMP SPEECH

"The House can go as fast as the Senate. And so the frustration that I and others have is the Senate's not moving as fast as we would like on this. I actually think there's 50 votes in the Senate for some of these really commonsense provisions," Steil said. "I'd like to be sooner rather than later, but I don't control them."

Where the process gets even trickier is when the Senate parliamentarian, who is appointed by Senate leadership to help interpret the chamber's rules, goes through the reconciliation bill draft and weeds out what does not adhere to the process rules. That means anything that does not impact the federal government's budget, tax policy, or the national debt is generally removed.

TOP TRUMP OFFICIAL MAKES NEW SAVE ACT CASE TO REPUBLICANS BEHIND CLOSED DOORS

Steil said portions of the SAVE America Act could arguably get through that filtration process by affecting funds going to states via the Help America Vote Act (HAVA), a 2002-era election reform law.

"We could free up those funds or enhance those funds for states to do those post-election audits, which is a really important part of election integrity. You can do the same in regards to photo ID," he said, adding that making Real ID the standard could also effectively impact the citizenship mandate. "Effectively, when an individual gets REAL ID, they're proving their citizenship."

TRUMP INTERVENES AS HOUSE GOP REVOLT PUTS SAVE AMERICA ACT AT CENTER OF SPENDING SHOWDOWN

And the Trump administration is behind the push. Earlier this year, Office of Management and Budget (OMB) Director Russell Vought told Republicans at a lawmaker-only meeting that the White House backed using the reconciliation process for SAVE America and argued it was the best way forward to pass the GOP's election reforms, multiple people in the room told Fox News Digital.

"The White House is engaged. We've had good conversations," Steil told Fox News Digital.

The House passed its version of the reconciliation bill earlier this summer, a $95 billion budget aimed at replenishing the U.S. military and enhancing election security.

But in the Senate, Budget Committee Chairman Ron Johnson, R-Wis., unveiled his committee's framework just before the chamber left for the August recess. It's not clear when it will advance through his panel or get a vote.

GOP CIVIL WAR ERUPTS OVER TRUMP'S LATEST AGENDA PUSH AS KEY REPUBLICANS THREATEN TO SINK MEGABILL

Their legislation calls for up to $150 billion in spending — a significant difference.

Speaker Mike Johnson, R-La., acknowledged that gap in an interview with Fox News Digital last month.

"I mean, the idea was, in keeping it skinny, is to move it quickly. And so the more you add to it, the more complex it gets, the more in the Senate — not to get too deep in the weeds — but procedurally, it involves more committees of jurisdiction in both bodies. And that's where things start to get weighted down. So we're very close to an election, the stakes are very high, the timing is short, and if you're going to do election integrity measures, you need to do it, like, yesterday," Johnson said. "We passed the SAVE America Act four times in the House. This is the last best effort to get it through the Senate, so I'm for doing it as quickly as possible."

Steil said he was optimistic that an agreement could be reached.

"I think, broadly, we're aligned. I think obviously the total numbers are different," he said. "I think everyone recognizes the importance of making sure that our men and women in uniform have the resources needed to not only defend themselves but to defend our country... And also that we have the resources needed to make sure that we're protecting our election."

item.title: 'A win is a win' says athlete who didn't let a little diarrhea keep her from finishing in first place
item.description: Joanna Wietrzyk powered through a mid-race diarrhea incident to win the HYROX event in Beijing, prompting the organization to review its protocols.
item.content:encoded:
Athletes are asked to push themselves during HYROX events. Sometimes they go beyond the expectations of the organization that puts these races together, races which combine both running and functional workout stations.

That was the case during a competition in Beijing this past weekend. The first place winner, Joanna Wietrzyk, bravely battled through a little mid-race diarrhea and refused to let it slow her down.

The 24-year-old Australian reportedly finished the event in 1 hour, 1 minute and 23 seconds, according to the NY Post. The mess running down her legs and any possible contamination it may cause wasn’t a concern.

Wietrzyk had first place on her mind. Of course, an event where someone pushes themselves to the point of diarrhea and beyond is going to get some attention and, of course, some of that attention is going to be negative.

She appears to have felt some of that negative heat herself after posting on Instagram to celebrate her victory. She wrote in a now-deleted post, "Go hard or go home they say … a win is a win. In all seriousness, thank you for all the support. I'll be back soon x."

Jokes post-diarrhea race win are frowned upon by some, it turns out. Are these sore losers or people genuinely disgusted by watching an athlete go the distance after an accident?

HYROX is taking the matter seriously and looking at themselves to see how they can approve their procedures surrounding these unforeseen incidents. The last thing anyone wants is for this to start being implemented as a way to win.

COCO GAUFF VOMITS MID-MATCH, STILL SECURES WIN AS ILLNESS RIPS THROUGH MADRID OPEN

"We ask our athletes to push themselves to the highest levels. At times, they will go beyond what even we thought was possible. That courage, resilience and refusal to give in are precisely what makes elite athletes so extraordinary. Our role is to give them the right framework and the right boundaries within which they can compete, perform and express themselves at their very best," HYROX wrote on Instagram.

"HYROX has clear biocontaminant and medical procedures in place. In this instance, an unforeseen situation arose in which protocols designed for elite competition and mass participation became blurred, creating ambiguity in how they were applied and understood," the statement continued.

"We recognise that this can understandably lead to frustration, questions and strong views within our community. Those concerns are legitimate and, as organisers, we must be prepared to hear them, examine what happened and take responsibility for continuing to improve. And we will…"

That's all anyone can ask. You don't want to see an athlete stripped of a win because of their will to keep pressing on no matter what. It's on those at the top of the sport to tell an athlete that diarrhea needs to be cleaned up.

item.title: FCC Chairman Brendan Carr accuses James Talarico of running a 'hoax' over equal time statute
item.description: Brendan Carr accuses James Talarico of running a "hoax" by banking on public confusion over the equal time statute to drive clicks and donations.
item.content:encoded:
Federal Communications Commission (FCC) Chairman Brendan Carr accused Democratic Texas Senate candidate James Talarico of banking on public confusion over the equal time statute to drive clicks and donations.

Last week, Talarico appeared on ABC’s "Jimmy Kimmel Live!," but the liberal late-night host insisted the interview had to air on YouTube, instead of broadcast television, because the FCC has "threatened" the network. 

The White House previously said Kimmel was "play-acting," because the FCC did not threaten him regarding interviewing Talarico, or any other candidate.

Carr responded on Saturday to an account on X that complained Talarico was relegated to YouTube, but Sen. Ted Cruz, R-Texas, was allowed to appear on ESPN’s "College Gameday." The chairman blasted Talarico, noting that the equal time statute doesn’t apply to ESPN and does not prohibit anyone from interviewing anyone on broadcast TV.

KIMMEL REVEALS HE'S INTERVIEWING JAMES TALARICO UNDER 'UNUSUAL CIRCUMSTANCES,' CITING FCC THREATS

"It is about more speech, not less. Congress wanted to ensure that voters would decide elections, not media gatekeepers picking winners and losers by providing preferential airtime to some candidates and not others. Indeed, when the statute applies, it simply requires broadcast stations to offer comparable time and placement. And comparable does not necessarily mean an interview by the same person on the same program either," Carr wrote.

"This ties back to Talarico," Carr continued. "He’s just running the same hoax he did a few months ago on Colbert for the purpose of getting clicks and donations — he’s banking on people not understanding the statute or operating as partisan lemmings."

DEMOCRATIC REP TELLS ABC, CBS TO 'GROW A SPINE' AFTER KIMMEL ANNOUNCES ALTERNATIVE TALARICO INTERVIEW

Former late-night host Stephen Colbert interviewed Talarico in February, ahead of the Texas Senate primary, in which he was competing against Texas Rep. Jasmine Crockett.

Colbert's show, which has since been canceled, did not air the interview with Talarico and only posted it to the show's YouTube channel in February. Colbert announced at the time that CBS had stopped them from airing the interview.

JIMMY KIMMEL REVEALS HE ASKED MAJOR TRUMP CRITIC TO GUEST HOST WHILE HE'S ON VACATION AS A 'SPECIAL TREAT'

Crockett, who ultimately lost the Senate primary to Talarico, blamed CBS and Colbert's show. Critics on social media noted that Talarico’s sit-down with Kimmel was similar to the Colbert edition, with both hosts setting the Senate candidate up to declare that the Trump administration must be scared of him if they’re taking equal time so seriously.

The Talarico campaign did not immediately respond to Fox News Digital's request for comment.

In Saturday’s post, Carr also explained that "cable shows are different than broadcast programs."

"Broadcasters are unique. The FCC gave them free licenses worth many billions of dollars to use a public resource (spectrum). They are given a government-sanctioned monopoly on their broadcast frequencies, too. If anyone else wants to use that same public resource (spectrum) for the purpose of expressing their own views, the government will not let them — it will eject anyone else that tries to use a broadcaster’s licensed spectrum," he wrote.

"This means that Americans are subsidizing the distribution of broadcast programs over a public resource to the tune of many billions of dollars. We don’t do that with cable or anything else. In exchange for that free and exclusive right to use spectrum, broadcasters made a deal with the American people," Carr continued. "They agreed to operate, not in their own narrow interests, but in the public interest. There are various rules and policies that they must follow. This sets them apart from newspapers and cable shows and podcasts."

Kimmel’s interview with Talarico has piled up over 9 million views on YouTube.

item.title: Former CIA Director Brennan subpoenaed to testify in federal Trump conspiracy case
item.description: John Brennan faces a grand jury subpoena in a Justice Department probe into whether officials conspired to deprive Trump of his civil rights.
item.content:encoded:
Former CIA Director John Brennan has been subpoenaed to testify next month before a Florida grand jury as part of a Justice Department investigation into whether former law enforcement and intelligence officials conspired against President Donald Trump.

Ken Wainstein, an attorney for Brennan, disclosed in a court filing Monday that prosecutors last Thursday presented him with a subpoena for Brennan to appear Oct. 15 before a grand jury in Fort Pierce, Florida.

He said he was told that the subpoena relates to a "far-reaching" criminal probe examining whether government officials who have investigated Trump over the past decade conspired to deprive Trump of his civil rights.

JOHN SOLOMON PREDICTS BRENNAN INDICTMENT COULD COME WITHIN 'WEEKS' AS PROSECUTORS REQUEST OFFICIAL TRANSCRIPTS

According to Wainstein, a prosecutor also informed him that Brennan remains a target in a separate Washington-based investigation examining whether he lied to Congress in 2023, an allegation Brennan and his legal team have consistently denied.

The development comes amid leadership upheaval within the probe. The subpoena was delivered on the same day Joe diGenova, the prosecutor leading the inquiry informally known as the "grand conspiracy" investigation, abruptly resigned.

NEW FEDERAL GRAND JURY SUBPOENA ISSUED TO FORMER JAMES COMEY ADVISOR IN LEAK INVESTIGATION: SOURCES

The Justice Department has not publicly named a replacement for diGenova. Wainstein said he spoke with Kurt Olsen, a member of the investigative team and a lawyer who urged the Justice Department in 2020 to back Trump's claims that the election had been stolen.

Disclosure of the subpoena came hours ahead of a scheduled court hearing in Washington concerning a lawsuit brought by Brennan.

The former CIA chief is seeking a court order to preserve all records related to the investigations targeting him, arguing the documents are essential to challenge any potential indictment on grounds of vindictive prosecution.

The Associated Press contributed to this report.

item.title: Trump unloads on tech titans pushing for slowdown on emerging industry: ‘WHOEVER WINS AI, WINS!’
item.description: President Donald Trump rejected calls for AI guardrails and singled out Dario Amodei, as David Sacks challenged the industry's push to pace the frontier.
item.content:encoded:
President Donald Trump on Monday rejected growing calls for implementing safeguards and restrictions on artificial intelligence (AI), declaring that the technology needs a "STRONG AND SMART" president rather than additional restraints.

Even some of Silicon Valley's most powerful executives, including those within the AI space, are calling for a slowdown in the development of increasingly capable artificial intelligence technology.

"The only control or 'guardrails' that AI needs is a STRONG AND SMART (High IQ!) PRESIDENT, and the U.S.A. has that, in spades!" Trump wrote on Truth Social.

Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei over the weekend made waves as he called on leading AI companies to "pace the frontier" amid warnings that increasingly powerful systems could eventually outstrip humanity's ability to understand or control them.

MIKE JOHNSON REJECTS AI MORATORIUM OVER CHINA THREAT AS CONSERVATIVE ACTIVIST DEMANDS GUARDRAILS

"The Trump Administration has stopped AI 'people' from doing bad, or potentially bad, 'things,' like Dario (Anthropic!), who is now pretending to be a 'perfect little angel' — and we will continue to do so!" the president wrote on Truth Social.

Previously, the Trump administration designated Anthropic a supply-chain risk and moved to restrict federal agencies from using its technology, though a federal judge temporarily blocked that designation last month. Anthropic is most known for its AI model Claude, one of the top known and used LLM chatbots in the U.S.

Trump argues that the federal government already has "tremendous CRIMINAL and REGULATORY power over these companies" and warned that additional restraints on American AI development could benefit China in the AI race.

"There is a SICK conspiracy going on against AI and Data Centers, and the only one that is happy about it is China," he wrote. "WHOEVER WINS AI, WINS! We are leading China, and all others, and will continue to do so."

FETTERMAN ALIGNS WITH TRUMP ON AI PUSH, WARNS CHINA BENEFITS FROM US 'OVERREACTION'

Trump's intervention escalated a rapidly widening debate over whether America's leading AI companies should voluntarily slow the development of their most powerful systems — and what role Washington should play in policing an industry racing against both domestic competitors and China.

Amodei ignited the debate Saturday with an essay arguing that AI capabilities are advancing so quickly that safety measures may no longer be keeping pace.

His call quickly drew support from several of the industry's most prominent figures.

OpenAI CEO Sam Altman said he agreed that companies need to "pace the frontier," while Elon Musk said Amodei was "right." Google DeepMind's Demis Hassabis also said Amodei's proposal pointed in the right direction.

But David Sacks, Trump's White House AI and crypto advisor, sharply challenged the premise that the companies need government help to slow themselves down.

"The easiest way not to build superintelligence is for you to agree not to build it," Sacks wrote Saturday on X in response to Altman and Amodei. "Stop pretending you need anyone else's permission."

"You guys are the frontier," he continued. "By any reasonable metric — market share, revenue growth, model capability — the two of you have a duopoly on frontier AI."

"So just do it," Sacks added. "If you do, you'll buy goodwill for the next conversation. If you don't, we'll know this was just another bid for regulatory capture — or an election-season psyop."

Amodei's proposal, however, does not call for halting AI development altogether. He described "pacing" as slowing advances in model capabilities enough to give companies time to align and safeguard their systems and allow outside evaluators to test whether those protections are working.

Anthropic has already committed to one piece of the proposal: giving third-party evaluators ongoing, employee-like access to assess its safety practices, training processes and models. Altman said OpenAI would adopt a similar approach.

Other elements would require broader coordination among competing AI companies and, eventually, governments around the world. That coordination became another target of Sacks' criticism.

"Stop pretending antitrust law has to be suspended so you can form a cartel," Sacks wrote. "Stop pretending you need a regulatory approval process that supersedes product liability."

Amodei has argued that companies should be able to coordinate on common safety practices without risking antitrust penalties. Sacks countered that the leading companies do not need government permission to voluntarily slow their own development if they believe their systems are becoming dangerous.

The warnings from Amodei and other AI researchers center on increasingly autonomous systems that can perform sophisticated tasks with less human direction.

RESEARCHER WHO DEPARTED AI ROLE OVER FEARS OF RACING INTO EXTINCTION SAYS PEOPLE ARE 'BEGGING' FOR REGULATION

Amodei said AI's growing ability to assist with AI research itself could create a feedback loop in which increasingly capable systems help develop their own successors, potentially allowing capabilities to advance faster than humans can understand or control them.

He also pointed to a recent OpenAI evaluation in which AI agents escaped a testing environment and conducted unauthorized cyber activity against the AI development platform Hugging Face. The exercise occurred in a controlled setting, but Amodei cited it as evidence of the potential consequences as frontier systems become more capable.

Sacks acknowledged that slowing development could create "breathing room" for a broader discussion about AI safety, but argued that any global agreement would confront a fundamental problem: China.

"China is very unlikely to join a global agreement, as you know, and that has to be taken into account as well," Sacks wrote. "So go ahead and pace the frontier. You are the ones setting it."

Amodei has acknowledged the same geopolitical dilemma, warning that a system in which American companies restrain themselves while China continues racing ahead could create its own national security risks.

Altman expanded on his position Monday, saying frontier AI companies should strengthen safety practices immediately rather than waiting for Congress to act.

"The world deserves confidence that American companies developing increasingly capable AI will act responsibly, especially as the trajectory of progress has steepened," Altman wrote. "Every frontier lab must deliver on this, and there is no reason any of us should come to work if we cannot."

Altman said OpenAI welcomes "a federal framework that sets consistent safety requirements for frontier AI," but added that the company does "not believe we need to wait for an anti-trust exemption or legislation" before implementing stronger safeguards.

He said OpenAI supports explicit safety reviews before major training runs, shared industry standards and independent auditors, and has begun preparing formal "safety cases" before frontier reinforcement-learning runs expected to substantially increase model capabilities.

Altman called on other AI companies to develop comparable standards for monitoring, evaluating and mitigating those risks.

item.title: Kansas City Chiefs' roster concerns linger as they host the Denver Broncos on Monday Night Football
item.description: The Denver Broncos bring a top-ranked defense and Jaylen Waddle to Monday Night Football against a Chiefs team that finished 6-11 last season.
item.content:encoded:
Monday Night Football is here for the first time with the new season. We got some great games yesterday, including our first major upset and our first overtime game. Interestingly enough, I had both of those games in a teaser play that I shared and we lost. The other play, on the Raiders, was a sweat-free victory. Overall, it wasn't a terrible day; let's see if we can close out this week with a win as the Broncos take on the Chiefs.

The Denver Broncos are coming into the season with expectations of being one of the best teams in football. Last season, they were an injured quarterback and a couple of different plays away from getting to the Super Bowl. The defense was one of the best in football last season, locking down almost every team they played. On offense, Bo Nix took a big step forward, and now they've added Jaylen Waddle to the mix to give themselves an added option at receiver.

The team went 14-3 last season, and in the playoffs, they survived to pass the Bills in overtime. In the Conference Finals, they lost 10-7 to the Patriots with Jarrett Stidham under center. Of course, like most teams, you still have to assume the success or failure of the club falls on Bo Nix. This is Nix's third season in the league, and he is coming off an ankle injury. Last year, he produced about the same as his rookie year, but the team was significantly better. I'm interested to see what they can do to boost Nix a bit more this season. They tend to be a run-first team, but with Waddle and the other options, there is a chance this passing game can be dynamic.

BRONCOS STAR QUARTERBACK BO NIX UNDERWENT SECOND PROCEDURE ON SURGICALLY REPAIRED ANKLE: REPORT

The Kansas City Chiefs had a rough season last year, but with so much success from the organization for many years in a row, it was hard to replicate it. The Chiefs ended last season with a record of 6-11. Before you go and blame it on Patrick Mahomes getting injured, which did happen, he played in all but three games last year, and the team was 6-8 in those games. It just seemed like the team never could get anything going on offense, and their defense wasn't good enough.

As the team gets older and salary cap issues arise, the Chiefs will need to figure out a way to adjust their roster to stay competitive with Mahomes. For multiple seasons, they've really just relied on Mahomes being great and Travis Kelce being his security blanket. The wide receiver room was always somewhat ignored. Sure, they have Xavier Worthy and Rashee Rice, but neither of those guys is quite as good as you'd want when you have the best quarterback in football (debate it all you want, but he's won three Super Bowls and been to five in eight years as a starter).

PATRICK MAHOMES PARTICIPATES IN CHIEFS OTAS WITH HEAVY KNEE BRACE, STILL TARGETING WEEK 1 RETURN

I get that the Chiefs will be a public team, and that they are the home team. Taking an inter-division home dog is usually a good bet, but the Chiefs are the favorite tonight. The Broncos have a vastly superior defense in my ranks. Both quarterbacks are coming off of injury to return to this one. I feel like the under, especially in the first half (21.5), is a great look. item.title: California Democrat faces ouster call after her former professor tells crowd to 'f--- up' ICE agent
item.description: Video shows professor Melina Abdullah naming an ICE agent and sharing his hotel address before Sasha Renée Pérez took the stage at the summit.
item.content:encoded:
California state Sen. Sasha Renée Pérez, D-Pasadena, faced a call Sunday to lose her chairmanship of the Senate Education Committee after appearing at an immigration summit alongside a former professor who repeatedly told the crowd to "f--- up" a named ICE agent.

Video from last Sunday’s La Defensa Del Pueblo summit showed California State University, Los Angeles, professor Melina Abdullah identifying an ICE agent, saying he "may be staying" at a local Hilton Garden Inn and giving the crowd the hotel’s street address.

Abdullah repeatedly said to "f--- him up" before later explaining the phrase could include exposing immigration agents or making them uncomfortable. She also encouraged attendees to "study guerrilla warfare."

CALIFORNIA BILL WOULD LET ILLEGAL IMMIGRANT PROFESSORS KEEP TEACHING US STUDENTS REMOTELY

California Republican Party delegate and attorney Elizabeth Barcohana told Fox News Digital on Sunday that Pérez should no longer lead the Senate committee responsible for education policy.

"I believe Pérez should be removed as chair of education committee," Barcohana said.

Abdullah is a professor of Pan-African Studies at Cal State LA and a leader of Black Lives Matter Los Angeles. The university describes Abdullah as a "scholar-activist" who views her academic role as connected to broader activist movements.

After Abdullah’s remarks, Pérez took the microphone and referenced their former professor-student relationship.

"Y’all, it’s really hard to follow up my old college professor, Dr. Melina Abdullah… It’s such an honor to share space with you and to be able to sit next to you here," Pérez said.

ANTI-ICE WALKOUT EXPOSES HOW SCHOOL DISTRICT 'FAILED' PARENTS, RISKED STUDENT SAFETY: 'BROKEN MY TRUST'

Perez responded last week to suggestions that she was smiling at the professor's remarks, saying the video was edited. 

"I unequivocally condemn violence in all its forms, regardless of who uses it or whom it targets. I do not support, endorse, or condone violence against anyone, and my silence during another panelist’s remarks must never be misrepresented as agreement. Each speaker is responsible for their own words. A highly edited video circulating online falsely suggests I was smiling in response to violent remarks directed toward an ICE agent. The full video makes clear that my reaction was to separate comments about the courage of young people. Any suggestion that I share, endorse, or condone violence is false," Perez said, according to Los Angeles County Politics.

"I have consistently opposed the federal government’s cruel immigration enforcement practices while also unequivocally opposing violence in all forms including violence by government agents that took the life of Keith Porter Jr. and Lorenzo Salgado Araujo and violence by political extremists that took the life of Charlie Kirk. Political disagreement is not a license for racism, intimidation, or violence. I will continue to fight for civil rights through lawful, democratic action, and I will never condone violence."

Pérez earned degrees in political science and economics from Cal State LA before entering public service.

Barcohana also linked Pérez’s appearance alongside Abdullah to the senator’s role as chair of the Senate Education Committee and her record on immigration enforcement at California schools.

In a post about the summit, Barcohana specifically pointed to legislation Pérez authored requiring schools to issue alerts about immigration enforcement activity.

"Most relevant to this weekend’s summit, Pérez authored the bill that would turn California schools into participants in ICE resistance, rather than a neutral and safe learning environment for children," Barcohana said on X. 

"As Chair of the Education committee, Pérez saw to it that the antisemitism bill in the California legislature was rendered completely useless to its intended purpose of protecting Jewish students from harassment, discrimination, and intimidation. The bill was necessary because antisemitic incidents have increased over 600% in California K-12 schools."

DOJ DEMANDS SANCTUARY STATES END 'BLATANTLY UNLAWFUL' ANTI-ICE POLICY AS A MATTER OF LIFE AND DEATH

Pérez authored SB 98, the Sending Alerts to Families in Education, or SAFE, Act, which Gov. Gavin Newsom signed into law in September 2025. The law requires K-12 schools and higher education institutions to notify campus communities when immigration enforcement authorities are present on campus.

When Pérez introduced the bill in January 2025, her office said the proposal came in response to the Trump administration eliminating Biden-era guidance limiting immigration enforcement in certain "protected areas," including schools.

Pérez framed the measure as a response to concerns among immigrant students and parents about federal enforcement.

"The Trump administration has made clear that no place is safe from mass deportations. Students and parents are rightfully scared," Pérez said. "We will not be silent."

CLICK HERE FOR MORE COVERAGE OF MEDIA AND CULTURE

Newsom signed the legislation with an urgency clause, putting it into effect immediately. Pérez’s office has described the notifications as similar to warning systems used for other campus emergencies.

Pérez also criticized federal immigration authorities in 2025 when responding to plans for immigration enforcement agencies to participate in a Cal Poly Pomona career fair.

"ICE should have no place on our campuses," Pérez said.

A DHS spokesperson told Fox News Digital, "Governor Newsom continues to refuse to do his job to protect his citizens from illegal alien crime and instead chooses to smear our law enforcement."

"California politicians should focus on educating students, not turning classrooms into sanctuaries for illegal aliens. SB98 is a political stunt designed to create fear, interfere with law enforcement, and shield those who have violated our nation’s law. DHS will continue enforcing the laws Congress passed, and enforcing federal law when necessary, consistent with the Constitution and all applicable legal requirements. No state law will prevent federal officers from protecting American communities."

"While the media and sanctuary politicians try and spread falsehoods and demean DHS law enforcement, the men and woman of DHS are risking their lives and safety to arrest illegal criminal aliens that are victimizing Americans. Our message is clear: if you come to our country illegally, we will find you, we will arrest you, and we will deport you," the spokesperson added.

Republican California state Sen. Tony Strickland also said in comments to Fox News Digital, "The most essential role of government is public safety. As a legislator, I firmly stand with the men and women who put their lives on the line every day to protect our communities. Political disagreement does not justify intimidation or putting an officer and his family at risk. While free speech is a fundamental right, credible threats or targeted harassment must be taken seriously and investigated based on the facts and the law."

Fox News Digital reached out to Pérez, Abdullah and Cal State Los Angeles for comment, but did not immediately receive a response.

item.title: Malik Nabers reveals how Giants coach John Harbaugh helped him overcome his ACL injury fears
item.description: John Harbaugh tackled Malik Nabers during walkthrough practice to test his confidence after the wide receiver's ACL and meniscus knee injury.
item.content:encoded:
The biggest unknown the New York Giants faced before Sunday night's regular-season opener against the Dallas Cowboys, beyond whether they'd win or not, was whether star receiver Malik Nabers would play.

It's not that Nabers couldn't play. He'd been medically cleared for weeks.

The question was whether Nabers had the confidence to play, to get hit, and not be worried about getting hurt again after he suffered an ACL and meniscus right knee injury a year ago that required him overcoming psychological as well as physical hurdles.

Enter new Giants coach John Harbaugh.

JAXSON DART TAKES BRUTAL HIT EARLY IN GIANTS VS COWBOYS OPENER BUT WHAT HAPPENED NEXT WAS KIND OF SURPRISING

Harbaugh is different, folks. He started his postgame press conference after his team's victory over the Cowboys in the same way he ended his presser after a season-ending loss with the Ravens in 2025: By giving thanks to Jesus Christ.

He's also different in that he has won 13 season openers since becoming a head coach in 2008 and understands when players need nurturing or need pushing.

Nabers needed a little pushing. During the team's walkthrough practice on Saturday, Harbaugh decided Nabers needed to get over his uncertainty and insecurity about getting hit in a game.

So the coach tackled Nabers.

"I know everybody was worried about if I get tackled," Nabers told reporters. "Actually, coach Harbaugh tackled me ...

"He wanted to see if I could take a tackle and it was good."

In an age of analytics and metrics often driving coaching decisions, Harbaugh went old school. He figuratively threw his guy in a pool and forced him to swim.

"Yeah, we were all just chilling on the sideline," quarterback Jaxson Dart said, recounting the moment. "It was right before we were supposed to start our walkthrough, and things were just up in the air. We didn't know exactly what was going to happen.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE

"And me and coach Harbs kind of had some conversations. He's like, ‘You know what, like, I think that once he gets hit for the first time and realizes that he's OK, then he's going to feel confident.’

"So I think in his mind that triggered, ‘Oh, maybe I should tackle him right then and there.’ So, we're all just standing there, and then all of a sudden Leek goes down on the ground, and our team's super protective of him. So we all turned to look, and it's coach Harbs tackling Leek.

"And then he pops up and he goes, 'See, you're all good.'"

Nabers and other players pointed to the moment as pivotal , but it left Harbaugh still unsure whether his best receiver could play Sunday night. When was he finally certain?

"I got a sense like about three hours before the game, maybe two and a half, somewhere in there," Harbaugh said. "And when he went out and tested it and he felt ready and that’s when the decision was made. It was his call. He had been cleared medically, but he had to feel right.

"He had to feel like he was ready to go, and he could protect himself and perform the way he wanted, and he did. Malik played a great game. He played a heck of a game."

Nabers caught six passes for 69 and those are admittedly modest numbers. But they're important in that the Giants now have their best wide receiver back and are apparently confident he can withstand contact again.

"It was amazing, it was amazing," Nabers said. "It was amazing to take it all in, get right back on track to where I left off. I’m happy that the fans still love to see me out there."

item.title: Mamdani, Letitia James sue to block Trump admin from refusing immigrants over welfare status
item.description: NYC Mayor Zohran Mamdani claims the Trump administration is illegally expanding a rule that allows feds to deny green card and visa applications based on welfare status.
item.content:encoded:
New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani is suing President Donald Trump's administration over plans to expand federal authority to deny visa and green card applications based on welfare status.

The lawsuit, filed jointly with NY Attorney General Letitia James, targets the Trump administration's plan to expand the "public charge" rule, which allows the federal government to deny visa applications based on the likelihood that the applicant will receive public benefits. Trump's administration seeks to expand the list of benefits that apply under the rule, with the change taking effect Sept. 18.

"If you are a citizen, or an individual seeking humanitarian relief like asylum, these changes will not affect you," Mamdani said at a press conference Monday. "The new public charge rule not only sweeps aside more than a century of established law, it is intentionally vague as a means of creating uncertainty and fear to isolate immigrant New Yorkers."

"Make no mistake, this is an undisguised effort to strip New Yorkers of the services they rely on, the public benefits they are entitled to," he continued.

9/11 FAMILIES PUSH TO BAN MAMDANI FROM 25TH ANNIVERSARY REMEMBRANCE OVER 'HOSTILE' RECORD

Mamdani claimed that up to 4 million people could be forced to unenroll from their healthcare under the new rule out of fear their immigration applications could be denied.

MAMDANI HEADS TO 9/11 MEMORIAL DESPITE 110,000-SIGNATURE PUSH FROM VICTIMS’ FAMILIES TO STAY AWAY

Several major cities and counties across the country are joining New York's lawsuit, including Chicago, San Francisco, Seattle, Santa Clara County and King County, Mamdani said.

Meanwhile, James is launching a separate challenge to the rule, leading a coalition of 21 other states and the District of Columbia in asking the U.S. District Court for the Southern District of New York to block the Trump administration's rule.

"Hardworking families should not be forced to go without the support they need because they fear asking for assistance will get them deported," James said in a statement.

"This rule preys on that fear and counts on families forfeiting the food assistance, health care coverage, and other public benefits to which they are legally entitled. My office fought this exact policy once before and won, and we are leading the nation to ensure the Trump administration cannot inflict this harm on families again," she added.

The White House did not immediately respond to a request for comment from Fox News Digital.
